chunks: The time of the setting of the disc (sun) and the obligation of breaking the fast (iftar) is that you stand parallel to the Qibla and look for the redness which rises from the east. So when it has passed the top of the head toward the western direction, then the iftar has become obligatory and the disc (sun) has set.

key_terms.الْإِفْطَار: Iftar — the breaking of the obligatory fast at the end of the day
key_terms.الْحُمْرَة: The redness (eastern redness) — the red twilight that appears in the east after sunset, used as a celestial sign
key_terms.سُقُوطِ الْقُرْصِ: Setting of the solar disc — the true moment of sunset used as a legal marker
key_terms.قِمَّةَ الرَّأْس: Top of the head — the zenith point used as a reference for observing the eastward redness crossing overhead

ai.seo_question: How does one determine the time of Maghrib prayer and iftar according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a practical method for determining the time of Maghrib and when iftar becomes obligatory during Ramadan. The method involves standing facing the Qibla and observing the red glow that appears on the eastern horizon after sunset; when this redness passes overhead toward the west, the sun has truly set. This visual criterion was essential in a pre-clock era when Muslim communities needed a reliable, unaided way to determine the exact sunset time.
